claims.claim: Every connected cograph other than a singleton or a graph with exactly one universal vertex is equivalent to the zero game.
claims.evidence: In a reduced cotree, a connected cograph has a join root, and its singleton join blocks are exactly its universal vertices. With at least two universal vertices, pairing two of them covers every vertex by their closed-neighborhood intersection. With no universal vertex, every join block has at least two vertices; choosing a,b in one block and c,d in another gives disjoint pairs such that the first block lies in N[c]∩N[d] and every other vertex lies in N[a]∩N[b]. Thus a pairing dominating set exists, and the source's Remark 9 makes the component equivalent to zero. Exact minimax also confirmed all 1,199 applicable connected labeled cographs through six vertices and 144 tests after adjoining arbitrary small graph contexts.
claims.search_method: Reduced-cotree join-block case analysis, followed by exhaustive integer-bitmask minimax on bounded cographs and arbitrary small contexts.

claims.claim: SHVG on cographs is polynomially equivalent to an explicit open-or-delete scoring game on rooted forests.
claims.evidence: For a connected component with unique universal vertex u, swapping u with any proposed non-u move proves u weakly dominates that move for either player, even after adjoining an arbitrary disjoint position. If Breaker owns u, the component contributes zero. If Maker owns u, C-u has at least two vertices and hence a twin pair a,b; applying the source's Theorem 13 in both C with u Maker-owned and in C-u assigns a to Maker and b to Breaker. Then u is spoiled by b, while every vertex of C-u is happy in one position exactly when it is happy in the other. This proves the contextual open-or-delete transition. Recursion gives the forward forest. Conversely, adjoining a zero K2 ballast to the child realizations and then adding a universal cone vertex realizes each non-leaf project with L+3I vertices overall and at most quadratically many edges; nullary zero projects may simply be discarded. Exact minimax matched the forest reduction for all 6,039 labeled cographs through six vertices, verified the universal transitions in 228 arbitrary-context tests, and matched 16 independently generated reverse constructions.
claims.search_method: Contextual strategy transposition, twin-pair reduction, recursive cograph construction, and exhaustive exact minimax in both reduction directions.

claims.claim: The cograph game is linear-time solvable when every tree in the reduced forest has outdegree at most two.
claims.evidence: Inductively replace every child subtree by either the prize-leaf game A or zero. A root with zero or one A-child has both starting scores zero and is contextually zero. A root with two A-children lets Maker open to A+A, which is the constant game 1, while Breaker deletes to zero; these are exactly A's options, so the root is equivalent to A. Consequently the forest reduces to z copies of A, worth ceil(z/2) to Maker-first and floor(z/2) to Breaker-first. Cotree construction and bottom-up labeling process each vertex and edge only constantly many times. Exact minimax confirmed the formula on all 290 bounded-binary forests having at most eight nodes.
claims.search_method: Induction on reduced-tree height using contextual game equivalence, supplemented by exhaustive exact forest minimax.

claims.claim: Reduced forests of height one—equivalently, disjoint unions of stars and isolated vertices after zero components are removed—admit an O(n^2) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: For a multiset S of unopened star sizes and l exposed leaves, simultaneous induction on the remaining position proves leaf monotonicity, star-size monotonicity, and the exchange inequality V_X(S∪{j},l+k)≥V_X(S∪{k},l+j) for j≤k and either player X. Moves in S and exposed-leaf moves match to smaller induction instances; opening the distinguished stars produces the identical state with l+j+k leaves; deleting them uses monotonicity. The boundary j=l=0 reduces to a zero 0-star and leaf monotonicity. Hence Maker may open the largest star and Breaker may delete it, yielding exactly the displayed two-parameter recurrence. It has O(r(K+1)) states, with r,K≤n, and sorting is within O(n^2). Exact unrestricted minimax agreed with the recurrence on 125,840 states and separately confirmed 354,816 instances of the induction inequalities, including zero- and one-leaf stars.
claims.search_method: Completed simultaneous induction for monotonicity and the exposure-exchange law, plus exhaustive exact comparison of unrestricted and greedy recurrences.

claims.claim: The pair of standalone scores (Ms,Bs) is insufficient as a cotree dynamic-programming state.
claims.evidence: Exact minimax gives P3 and K1,3 the same standalone pair (1,0), but union with the same context P3 gives P3∪P3=(1,1) and P3∪K1,3=(2,1). Therefore equality of the two standalone scores is not preserved by the cotree union operation and cannot be a sufficient compositional state.
claims.witness: P3 has vertices {0,1,2} and edges {{0,1},{1,2}}; K1,3 has vertices {0,1,2,3} and edges {{0,1},{0,2},{0,3}}. Their exact scores are respectively P3=(1,0), K1,3=(1,0), P3∪P3=(1,1), and P3∪K1,3=(2,1).
claims.search_method: Direct integer-bitmask minimax on the two components and their disjoint unions with P3.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for either a polynomial-time algorithm on all cographs or a matching hardness theorem. The verified reduction only transfers the unrestricted case to an open-or-delete game on arbitrary rooted forests, while the two algorithms cover only bounded-outdegree and height-one forests. The final writeup explicitly states that arbitrary reduced forests remain unresolved and describes the result as partial. Thus it provides material correct progress but not the requested classification, and claimed_resolution=PARTIAL is accurate.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source-input JSON and iteration-2 draft; no web, retrieval database, receipt, prior run, report, or other solution was used.
Independently checked exact target coverage before auditing the individual claims.
Re-derived the cotree pairing certificates, contextual universal-vertex transpositions, twin reduction, reverse construction, binary-tree collapse, and height-one ordering recurrence.
Ran fresh integer-bitmask minimax on all 6,039 labeled cographs through six vertices; every graph matched its reduced forest.
Checked 1,199 connected zero cases, 144 arbitrary-context zero-component cases, and 228 arbitrary-context unique-universal cases.
Checked 16 reverse constructions, all 290 bounded-binary forests through eight nodes, 125,840 height-one states, and 354,816 height-one auxiliary inequalities.
Reproduced the four exact scores constituting the standalone-state counterexample.
All computational decisions used exact integers and bitmasks; no floating-point arithmetic was used.
